title: Correlation indicator R_p for quantifying overlap of large-magnitude weights
content:
Define the correlation indicator $R_p(\theta,\theta')$ for two weight collections $\theta$ and $\theta'$ in an $L$-layer network as
      $$
      R_p(\theta,\theta') = \frac{\sum_{l=1}^L \mathrm{card}\big(T_p(\theta^l) \cap T_p((\theta')^l)\big)}{p \cdot \sum_{l=1}^L N_l},
      $$
      where for layer $l$ with $N_l$ weights the set $T_p(\theta^l)$ is the indices of the top-$p\cdot 100\%$ largest-magnitude weights in that layer (for sparse networks $p$ is measured relative to the remaining weights). The indicator satisfies: if $R_p(\theta,\theta')\approx p$ then the two top-$p$ sets are approximately independent; deviations $R_p(\theta,\theta')>p$ ($<p$) indicate positive (negative) overlap beyond chance.

title: Empirical presence of winning property only at low learning rates (example: ResNet-20 CIFAR-10)
content: Under iterative magnitude pruning with weight reset to initialization (uniform per-layer pruning rate, first convolutional layer not pruned), using SGD with momentum 0.9 and a step learning rate schedule that decays by a factor of 10 at epochs 80 and 120 for a total of 150 epochs, the empirical winning property is observed for ResNet-20 on CIFAR-10 at an initial learning rate of 0.01 but not at 0.1. The winning property requires that training the masked initialization $\theta_0\odot m$ (where $\theta_0$ is the initial weight collection and $m$ is the binary pruning mask derived from the pretrained weights $\theta_T$) for 150 epochs yields higher accuracy than training the masked random reinitialization $\theta_0'\odot m$ (where $\theta_0'$ is a fresh random initialization) and approaches the accuracy of the pretrained dense model $\theta_T$. At learning rate 0.01, the pretrained dense accuracy is 89.62%; the winning ticket sparse training exceeds random reinitialization across sparsities and attains 90.04% at 62% sparsity. At learning rate 0.1, the pretrained dense accuracy is 91.7%; the winning ticket and random reinitialization have similar accuracy and neither reaches the pretrained dense accuracy at moderate or higher sparsities (e.g., 50% and beyond).

title: Empirical measurement: initial-to-final weight overlap is large at low learning rate and near-chance at higher learning rate
content: For a network with $L$ layers where layer $l$ has $N_l$ weights, let $T_p(\theta^l)$ be the set of indices of the top $p\cdot100\%$ largest-magnitude weights in $\theta^l$. The correlation indicator is $R_p(\theta,\theta') = \frac{\sum_{l=1}^L \mathrm{card}(T_p(\theta^l) \cap T_p((\theta')^l))}{p \cdot \sum_{l=1}^L N_l}$. When $R_p(\theta,\theta')$ significantly exceeds $p$, there is positive overlap beyond chance; when approximately equal to $p$, the sets are approximately independent. Using this indicator on ResNet-20 trained for 150 epochs on CIFAR-10 (SGD with momentum 0.9, step decay at 80 and 120 epochs by factor 10), the overlap $R_p(\theta_0,\theta_T)$ between the initial weights $\theta_0$ and the final pretrained weights $\theta_T$ is significantly larger than $p$ for initial learning rate 0.01 across $p=10\%,20\%,30\%,40\%,50\%$, indicating positive dependence between initialization and final weights; for initial learning rate 0.1 the measured $R_p(\theta_0,\theta_T)\approx p$, indicating approximate independence. Thus smaller learning rates produce stronger preserved rank-order of large-magnitude weights from initialization to the trained model.

title: Weight-correlation chain explains the winning property: correlation between $\theta_0$ and $\theta_T$ is a key condition
content: For a network with $L$ layers where layer $l$ has $N_l$ weights, define $R_p(\theta,\theta') = \frac{\sum_{l=1}^L \mathrm{card}(T_p(\theta^l) \cap T_p((\theta')^l))}{p \cdot \sum_{l=1}^L N_l}$ where $T_p(\theta^l)$ is the set of indices of the top $p\cdot100\%$ largest-magnitude weights in $\theta^l$. The winning property (training the masked initialization $\theta_0\odot m$ for $T$ epochs yields higher accuracy than training the masked random reinitialization $\theta_0'\odot m$ and approaches the accuracy of the pretrained dense model $\theta_T$) requires a chain of positive overlaps: first, a positive correlation between initialization and final pretrained dense weights ($R_p(\theta_0,\theta_T) > p$) implies a positive overlap between the masked initialization and the masked pretrained weights ($R_p(\theta_0\odot m, \theta_T\odot m) > p$). Second, because the pruned-and-fine-tuned weights $(\theta_T\odot m)_T$ (obtained by applying mask $m$ to $\theta_T$ and then fine-tuning for $T$ epochs) remain close to $\theta_T\odot m$, there is a positive overlap between $\theta_0\odot m$ and $(\theta_T\odot m)_T$. Under these conditions, at a low learning rate (e.g., 0.01) that slows weight updates, the masked initialization $\theta_0\odot m$ is closer to a reasonable solution than $\theta_0'\odot m$, so training from $\theta_0\odot m$ attains higher accuracy. At a desirable higher learning rate (e.g., 0.1), the initial-to-final correlation $R_p(\theta_0,\theta_T)\approx p$ is minor, this chain breaks, and winning tickets do not appear.

title: Pruning & fine-tuning (apply mask to $\theta_T$ then fine-tune) consistently outperforms sparse training from initialization under equal masks and epochs
content: For a fixed mask $m$ generated from the pretrained dense weights $\theta_T$ using a given pruning algorithm, and under the same total number of training epochs (150 epochs of pretraining to obtain $\theta_T$, followed by 150 epochs of either (a) sparse training from $\theta_0\odot m$ (winning ticket) or $\theta_0'\odot m$ (random reinitialization), or (b) pruning & fine-tuning from $\theta_T\odot m$), the pruning & fine-tuning workflow yields substantially higher accuracy across multiple architectures (VGG-11, ResNet-20, MobileNet-v2) and datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100) at initial learning rate 0.1. For example, on ResNet-20/CIFAR-10 with iterative magnitude pruning, pruning & fine-tuning restores pretrained dense accuracy at sparsities where the winning ticket and random reinitialization do not; with ADMM-based pruning, pruning & fine-tuning can restore or exceed the pretrained dense accuracy at up to 80% sparsity in some tested settings.

title: Pruning mask quality matters: ADMM-based > iterative > one-shot in downstream sparse accuracy
content: Under the same training protocol (150 epochs of pretraining at initial learning rate 0.1 with SGD and step decay, followed by 150 epochs of fine-tuning or sparse training from the reset point) on VGG-11, ResNet-20, and MobileNet-v2 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, the choice of mask-generation algorithm substantially affects final sparse accuracy. The rank order of mask quality, consistent across both pruning & fine-tuning and sparse training from initialization, is: ADMM-based pruning (best) > iterative magnitude pruning (middle) > one-shot magnitude pruning (worst). This indicates that mask quality is a primary determinant of achievable sparse accuracy under a fixed training budget.

title: Final sparse trained weights correlate with pretrained weights, not with initialization (numeric overlap table)
content: For a network with $L$ layers where layer $l$ has $N_l$ weights, define $R_p(\theta,\theta') = \frac{\sum_{l=1}^L \mathrm{card}(T_p(\theta^l) \cap T_p((\theta')^l))}{p \cdot \sum_{l=1}^L N_l}$, where $T_p(\theta^l)$ is the set of indices of the top $p\cdot100\%$ largest-magnitude weights in $\theta^l$. For pruning & fine-tuning at 50% sparsity on VGG-11, ResNet-20, and MobileNet-v2 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 (using ADMM-generated masks, initial learning rate 0.1, $T=150$), the overlap indicator at $p=20\%$ satisfies $R_{p}((\theta_T\odot m)_T,\theta_0)\approx 20\%$ while $R_{p}((\theta_T\odot m)_T,\theta_T)$ is substantially larger, ranging from 48% to 64% across the tested models and datasets. Thus the final sparse weights obtained by pruning & fine-tuning retain strong overlap with the pretrained dense weights $\theta_T$ but not with the random initialization $\theta_0$, indicating that desirable sparse solutions align with the pretrained solution rather than with initialization.

title: Pruning & fine-tuning outperforms intermediate-weight rewinding (Frankle et al. 2019) when total epochs are equal
content: Under equal total training epochs (150 epochs of pretraining followed by 150 epochs of training from the reset point) and using ADMM-generated masks derived from the pretrained dense model $\theta_T$, training from $\theta_T\odot m$ (pruning & fine-tuning) yields higher final test accuracy than training from $\theta_k\odot m$ (rewinding to weights $\theta_k$ after $k$ epochs of training from $\theta_0$) and than training from $\theta_0\odot m$ (winning ticket reset to initialization). Empirically, with $k=10$ and $T=150$ on VGG-11, ResNet-20, and MobileNet-v2 on CIFAR-100, the ordering of final accuracy is $(\theta_T\odot m)_T$ (best), $(\theta_k\odot m)_T$ (middle), $(\theta_0\odot m)_T$ (worst).
